name: crodh mara

attributes.attribute: kept by fairies in the ocean deeps
came ashore to mate with mortal cows
often red, sometimes gray or dun
haunts fresh and salt water on the west coast of Scotland
generally dun, near Skye red and speckled though described as black

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Highlanders called these fairy beasts crodh mara, the cattle of the sea. The name is Scottish Gaelic. The cattle dwelt in the ocean deeps and belonged to the fairies. They haunted fresh and salt water along the west coast of Scotland. The cattle could leave the sea and pair with ordinary cows. Their bulls mated with mortal cows, and the pairing bettered the herds of the land. The cattle carried no horns. Most wore a dun coat. Animals near Skye ran red and speckled, though people there described them as black. These sea cattle were gentler kin of the each uisce, the water horse. Welsh storytellers knew kindred beasts as Gwartheg y Llyn.

okr.objective: crodh mara are the Gaelic fairy cattle of the sea, haunting the west coast of Scotland.
key_results: The name is Scottish Gaelic for cattle of the sea.
The hornless cattle generally wore dun coats, with red speckled stock near Skye.
Their bulls mated with mortal cows and improved earthly herds.
They were gentler than the each uisce and had Welsh kin in Gwartheg y Llyn.
